name: Ho Chi Minh City
provinceNote: The city now includes the former Ba Ria–Vung Tau and Binh Duong provinces. The center visitors walk is still District 1.
summary: Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam’s largest city and the usual end of a north-to-south trip. District 1 holds the Opera House, Dong Khoi, and Ben Thanh Market. Three days covers the center, a museum, and either Cu Chi or a delta day.
fee: Walking is free; museums and Cu Chi are ticketed
getThere: Tan Son Nhat Airport is inside the city, often 30–60 minutes to District 1
seoTitle: Ho Chi Minh City travel guide — what to do, how to get there, where to eat
seoDescription: How to spend three days in Ho Chi Minh City, where to stay in District 1, and which day trips are worth leaving town for.
intro: The city is still called Saigon by many residents, and that name fits the center: a tight commercial downtown that grew under French rule and then kept growing. The walkable visitor core is District 1. Cholon, the Chinese commercial district, is a separate half-day.

Eat com tam, broken rice, and a bowl of pho in the south’s sweeter style. Use the War Remnants Museum if you want the documentary record, and allow time; it is not a light hour. The Reunification Palace is the other standard stop, a preserved 1960s government building.
gettingAround: Tan Son Nhat is close by Asian-capital standards and still slow at rush hour. GrabCar is the default. Walking works inside District 1 if you treat motorbike traffic as the rule of the road: cross with a steady pace, not a dash.
The first metro line is useful on its own corridor and does not link every sight. For Cu Chi and the delta, book a car or a tour rather than improvising at the bus station with luggage.

stayAreas.name: District 1
stayAreas.summary: The practical base. Walk to dinner. Book a street set back from the night clubs if you want sleep.

stayAreas.name: District 3
stayAreas.summary: Quieter streets, a short ride from the center, better if you want local cafes.

eat: Southern food is sweeter and more herb-heavy. Com tam, banh xeo, hu tieu, and a late bowl of pho are the city set.
Ben Thanh’s stalls are convenient and priced for visitors. Walk a few blocks to a com tam room with a lunch queue.
interestsBody: Food, markets, and the city’s war-history museums. The beach is not here; Vung Tau and Phu Quoc are separate rides or flights.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: The southern table is sweeter, herbier, and built around rice plates as much as noodle soups. Com tam is the lunch. Banh xeo is the shared snack.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Conical hats and lacquer in Ben Thanh, and a downtown mall on Lê Thánh Tôn. The published clocks do not match.

blocks.heading: Ben Thanh Market
paragraphs: The city tourism plan puts the main door on Quách Thị Trang Square, the north gate on Lê Thánh Tôn, the east gate on Phan Bội Châu, and the west gate on Phan Chu Trinh. It says the market was established in 1914, on 13,056 m², and it prints 07:00 to 19:00 every day, with a night market from 19:00 to 24:00. Vietnam Tourism’s attractions page prints a different clock, 07:30 to 12:00 and 13:30 to 17:00, and the address 32-30 Phan Bội Châu. Admission on that page is free. The hours are check on arrival until the two pages agree.

That Vietnam Tourism page says the aisles sell fresh produce, conical hats, weasel coffee, and lacquerware. The food stalls at the end of the hall are a meal, and they stay on the food guide. No stall price is printed. Agree a figure before you pay. The price is check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Vincom Center Đồng Khởi
paragraphs: Vincom’s mall directory lists Vincom Center Đồng Khởi at 72 Lê Thánh Tôn, Bến Nghé ward, District 1, and prints one clock, 09:30 to 22:00. The center’s introduction page, updated 11 September 2026, gives 72 Lê Thánh Tôn and 45A Lý Tự Trọng, phường Sài Gòn. That page prints 10:00 to 22:00 every day in the short facts, and a different split in the hour table: 10:00 to 22:00 Monday to Wednesday, and 09:30 to 22:00 on the other days. The hours are check on arrival.

The introduction calls it a shopping center on the Đồng Khởi and Lê Thánh Tôn corner, with fashion and cosmetics on the upper floors. The food hall is a meal, and it stays on the food guide. No door fee is printed. Entry is check on arrival.

cards.title: Ben Thanh Market
cards.summary: Conical hats, lacquerware, and weasel coffee in the aisles. Admission is free on the Vietnam Tourism page. The city plan prints 07:00 to 19:00 and a night market to 24:00. The other page prints a split daytime clock. Check the board.

cards.title: Vincom Center Đồng Khởi
cards.summary: A shopping center at 72 Lê Thánh Tôn, on the Đồng Khởi corner. The directory prints 09:30 to 22:00. The introduction page, updated 11 September 2026, does not use that same clock. Check the board.

cards.title: War Remnants Museum
cards.summary: A direct, photographic museum of the wars in Vietnam. It is distressing and crowded. Read it slowly or not at all.

cards.title: Reunification Palace
cards.summary: The former presidential palace, kept as it was in 1975, including the war rooms.

Cholon, the Chinese commercial district, is a separate half-day. It has no licensed photograph here, so it is not a card.

faqs.q: Is Ho Chi Minh City the same as Saigon?
faqs.a: Saigon is the older name and still the everyday name for the center. Ho Chi Minh City is the official name, and after 2025 it covers a wider area than the downtown you will walk.

faqs.q: How many days do you need?
faqs.a: Three days for the center and one excursion. Add a night in Can Tho if the delta is more than a checkbox.
